intro: Hi! You already say what's happening now: I'm cooking. Today you take 'sedang' into the past: At 8 last night I was cooking. It's was/were + -ing, for something that was in the middle of happening at a time in the past. Warm-up: what were you doing at 8 last night? Try 'I was …'.
teachingNotes: Form: was/were + verb-ing. Indonesian marks this with 'sedang' + a past time word (Jam 8 tadi malam saya sedang memasak) and never changes the verb, so the #1 errors are keeping am/is/are with a past time (*'At 8 last night I am cooking' → 'I was cooking') and dropping -ing after was (*'At 8 I was have dinner' → 'was having', *'I was cook'). Also watch for no be at all (*'I cooking').

was or were: the same choice as the past of to be. I/he/she/it and one person or thing → was; you/we/they and two or more → were. The classic error is *'They was watching TV': they = more than one → were. 'you' is always were, even for one person (because it's 'you are' in the present). Suggest a quick test: replace the subject with he/she/they.

-ing spelling is the same as in the present continuous lesson: add -ing (cook → cooking, study → studying), drop a final e (make → making, have → having), double the last letter of one-beat verbs ending one vowel + one consonant (run → running, sit → sitting, swim → swimming, chat → chatting). Don't add new spelling rules (lie → lying, begin → beginning).

Negatives and questions work like was/were alone: wasn't/weren't + -ing; Was/Were + subject + -ing? Short answers: Yes, she was. / No, they weren't. Key question: What were you doing at …? (Kamu sedang apa jam …?). Never did: *'Did you sleeping?', *'Did you was sleeping?'. Watch for statement order with a question mark (*'You were sleeping?').

Use: an action in progress (already started, not finished) at a specific past time: at 8 last night, at 7 this morning, at this time yesterday, at 3 yesterday afternoon. Contrast with the past simple only in clear cases: past simple = the whole finished action (I cooked dinner last night, Rina went to Jakarta last week); past continuous = in the middle at that moment. A timeline helps: started 7:30 → at 8 in the middle → finished 8:30. Don't test sentences where both tenses are possible.

Limits: 'when/while' interruptions (I was cooking when Budi came) may be mentioned as a pattern they'll meet later, but never drilled or tested. No present perfect, past perfect or 'was going to'. If a learner asks about *'I was knowing' or *'I was wanting', just say know/like/want usually stay in the simple form; don't go deeper.

keyPoints.title: was / were + -ing
keyPoints.explanation: To say what was happening in the past, use was/were + verb-ing. I, he, she, it and one person → was; you, we, they and two or more people → were (never 'they was'). Keep the -ing, spelled as in the present continuous: having, running, studying. Negative: wasn't/weren't + -ing. Question: Was/Were + subject + -ing? No did.

examples.en: Dimas was sleeping on the sofa.
The students weren't listening to the teacher.
examples.id: Para murid tidak sedang mendengarkan guru.

examples.en: Was it raining in Bogor? — Yes, it was.
examples.id: Apakah di Bogor sedang hujan? — Ya.

id.title: was / were + -ing
id.explanation: Untuk bilang apa yang sedang terjadi di masa lalu, pakai was/were + kata kerja-ing. I, he, she, it dan satu orang → was; you, we, they dan dua orang atau lebih → were (tidak pernah 'they was'). -ing-nya tetap, dengan ejaan seperti di present continuous: having, running, studying. Negatif: wasn't/weren't + -ing. Pertanyaan: Was/Were + subjek + -ing? Tanpa did.

keyPoints.title: In the middle at a past time
keyPoints.explanation: Use the past continuous for an action that was in progress at a time in the past: it had started and wasn't finished yet. At 8 last night I was cooking. Indonesian says 'sedang' + a time word, but English also changes am/is/are to was/were: not 'At 8 last night I am cooking'. The past simple (I cooked) tells the whole finished action.

examples.en: At 8 last night I was cooking.
examples.id: Jam 8 tadi malam saya sedang memasak.

examples.en: At this time yesterday we were sitting on a train.
examples.id: Kemarin jam segini kami sedang duduk di kereta.

examples.en: What were you doing at 10 last night?
examples.id: Kamu sedang apa jam 10 tadi malam?

id.title: Sedang berlangsung pada waktu lampau
id.explanation: Pakai past continuous untuk kegiatan yang sedang berlangsung pada suatu waktu di masa lalu: sudah dimulai dan belum selesai. At 8 last night I was cooking. Bahasa Indonesia bilang 'sedang' + kata waktu, tapi bahasa Inggris juga mengganti am/is/are dengan was/were: bukan 'At 8 last night I am cooking'. Past simple (I cooked) menceritakan seluruh kegiatan yang sudah selesai.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the past continuous of 'wait': At nine last night my parents ___ for me at the station.
acceptableAnswers: were waiting
assessment.rubric: Correct: were waiting. 'was waiting' = 50 (my parents = they → were). 'were wait' = 40 (missing -ing). 'waiting' alone = 30 (missing were). 'are waiting' = 30 (present; nine last night is past). 'waited' = 30 (not the past continuous).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake (keep 'was'): At 7 this morning Sari was have breakfast.
acceptableAnswers: at 7 this morning sari was having breakfast
at seven this morning sari was having breakfast
sari was having breakfast at 7 this morning
sari was having breakfast at seven this morning
assessment.rubric: Correct: At 7 this morning Sari was having breakfast. 'was haveing' = 70 (drop the e). 'was had' = 20. 'had breakfast' without was = 40 (the task says keep was). Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Make it negative: The children were sleeping at ten.
acceptableAnswers: the children weren't sleeping at ten
the children were not sleeping at ten
the children weren't sleeping at 10
the children were not sleeping at 10
assessment.rubric: Correct: The children weren't / were not sleeping at ten. 'wasn't sleeping' = 50 (children = they → were). 'weren't sleep' = 40 (missing -ing). 'didn't sleeping' or 'didn't sleep' = 30. 'not sleeping' without were = 20.

assessment.prompt: Make a question: Your brother was playing games at midnight.
acceptableAnswers: was your brother playing games at midnight
assessment.rubric: Correct: Was your brother playing games at midnight? 'Were your brother…' = 50 (one person → was). 'Was your brother play…' = 40 (missing -ing). 'Did your brother playing…' = 20. Statement order with a question mark = 20.

assessment.prompt: Translate: Jam sembilan tadi malam Budi sedang menyetir ke Bandung.
acceptableAnswers: at nine last night budi was driving to bandung
at 9 last night budi was driving to bandung
budi was driving to bandung at nine last night
budi was driving to bandung at 9 last night
at 9 pm last night budi was driving to bandung
budi was driving to bandung at 9 pm last night
last night at nine budi was driving to bandung
last night at 9 budi was driving to bandung
assessment.rubric: Correct: At nine last night Budi was driving to Bandung. 'is driving' = 30 (the sedang trap: nine last night is past → was). 'was drive' = 40 (missing -ing). 'drove' = 50 (past, but sedang = in progress → was driving). 'were driving' = 60. Missing 'last night' = 70.

assessment.prompt: Complete with 'study': Budi: 'What were you doing at 8 last night?' Sari: 'I ___ for my exam.'
acceptableAnswers: was studying
i was studying
assessment.rubric: Correct: was studying ('What were you doing at 8?' asks about the middle of an action at a past time). 'was studing' = 70 (spelling: study + ing). 'were studying' = 50 (I → was). 'studied' = 40. 'am studying' = 30 (present). 'was study' = 40.

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake in the answer: 'What were you doing at 4 p.m. last Sunday?' — 'We are swimming at the pool.'
acceptableAnswers: we were swimming at the pool
we were swimming at the pool at 4 pm last sunday
at 4 pm last sunday we were swimming at the pool
assessment.rubric: Correct: We were swimming at the pool (last Sunday is past; the question asks what was in progress). 'We was swimming' = 50 (we → were). 'We were swim' = 40. 'We swam at the pool' = 40 (past, but the question asks what you were in the middle of). 'We were swiming' = 70. Unchanged = 0.

blocks.text:
You know the present continuous: **I'm cooking** = *saya sedang memasak* (now). To talk about the past, change **am / is / are** to **was / were** and keep the **-ing**: **At 8 last night I was cooking.** This is the **past continuous**: an action that was **in progress** at a time in the past (it had already started, and it wasn't finished yet).

The Indonesian trap: Indonesian uses the same *sedang* for now and for the past: *Saya sedang memasak* and *Jam 8 tadi malam saya sedang memasak*. Only the time word shows the past. English changes the helper word too: **am → was**. So *At 8 last night I am cooking* is wrong: 8 last night is already in the past → **I was cooking**.

id.text:
Kamu sudah kenal present continuous: **I'm cooking** = *saya sedang memasak* (sekarang). Untuk masa lalu, ganti **am / is / are** dengan **was / were**, dan -ing-nya tetap: **At 8 last night I was cooking.** Ini namanya **past continuous**: kegiatan yang **sedang berlangsung** pada suatu waktu di masa lalu (sudah dimulai, tapi belum selesai).

Jebakan dari bahasa Indonesia: kita memakai *sedang* yang sama untuk sekarang dan untuk masa lalu: *Saya sedang memasak* dan *Jam 8 tadi malam saya sedang memasak*. Hanya kata waktunya yang menunjukkan masa lalu. Bahasa Inggris juga mengubah kata bantunya: **am → was**. Jadi *At 8 last night I am cooking* itu salah: jam 8 tadi malam sudah lewat → **I was cooking**.

rows.en: At 8 last night I was cooking.
rows.id: Jam 8 tadi malam saya sedang memasak.

rows.en: At 3 yesterday afternoon Sari was working at the bank.
rows.id: Kemarin jam 3 sore Sari sedang bekerja di bank.

rows.en: At this time yesterday we were sitting on a train to Bandung.
rows.id: Kemarin jam segini kami sedang duduk di kereta ke Bandung.
rows.note: at this time yesterday = kemarin jam segini

id.note: at this time yesterday = kemarin jam segini

rows.note: it means nothing here, like in It's raining

id.note: it di sini tidak ada artinya, sama seperti di It's raining

blocks.text: Two common mistakes: keeping **am/is/are** with a past time (*At 8 last night I am cooking*) and dropping the **-ing** (*I was cook*, *I was have dinner*). A past time needs **was/were**, and the verb always needs **-ing**: **I was having dinner**. (*have dinner* = makan malam, an action, so it can take -ing, like *having lunch*.)

id.text: Dua kesalahan yang sering terjadi: tetap memakai **am/is/are** dengan waktu lampau (*At 8 last night I am cooking*) dan menghilangkan **-ing** (*I was cook*, *I was have dinner*). Waktu lampau butuh **was/were**, dan kata kerjanya selalu butuh **-ing**: **I was having dinner**. (*have dinner* = makan malam, sebuah kegiatan, jadi boleh pakai -ing, seperti *having lunch*.)

blocks.prompt: Which sentence means 'Kemarin jam 5 sore Budi sedang bermain futsal'?
options: At 5 yesterday afternoon Budi is playing futsal.
At 5 yesterday afternoon Budi was playing futsal.
At 5 yesterday afternoon Budi was play futsal.
blocks.explain: 5 yesterday afternoon is in the past, so is becomes was, and the verb keeps -ing: was playing. 'is playing' keeps the present (the sedang habit), and 'was play' drops the -ing.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang artinya 'Kemarin jam 5 sore Budi sedang bermain futsal'?
id.explain: Jam 5 kemarin sore sudah lewat, jadi is menjadi was, dan kata kerjanya tetap -ing: was playing. 'is playing' tetap bentuk sekarang (kebiasaan dari kata sedang), dan 'was play' kehilangan -ing.

blocks.text:
Choose **was** or **were** exactly as you do for the past of *to be*:
- **I, he, she, it**, and **one** person or thing (*Rina, my boss, the baby*) → **was**
- **you, we, they**, and **two or more** people or things (*my parents, Budi and Sari*) → **were**

**They was** is wrong: *they* is more than one person, so it's always **they were**. Indonesian has no was/were (*dia sedang menonton* and *mereka sedang menonton* use the same *sedang*), so look at the **subject** (who does the action) every time. **you** is always **were**, even for one person, because it's *you are* in the present (an exception to remember).

The **-ing** spelling is the same as in the present continuous: just add -ing (*cook → cooking, study → studying*), drop a final -e (*make → making, have → having*), and double the last letter of short verbs like *run → running, sit → sitting, swim → swimming*.

id.text:
Pilih **was** atau **were** persis seperti pada bentuk lampau *to be*:
- **I, he, she, it**, dan **satu** orang atau benda (*Rina, my boss, the baby*) → **was**
- **you, we, they**, dan **dua atau lebih** orang atau benda (*my parents, Budi and Sari*) → **were**

**They was** itu salah: *they* lebih dari satu orang, jadi selalu **they were**. Bahasa Indonesia tidak punya was/were (*dia sedang menonton* dan *mereka sedang menonton* memakai *sedang* yang sama), jadi selalu lihat **subjeknya** (siapa yang melakukan kegiatan). **you** selalu memakai **were**, walaupun hanya satu orang, karena di bentuk sekarang juga *you are* (pengecualian yang perlu diingat).

Ejaan **-ing** sama seperti di present continuous: cukup tambah -ing (*cook → cooking, study → studying*), buang -e di akhir (*make → making, have → having*), dan gandakan huruf terakhir kata kerja pendek seperti *run → running, sit → sitting, swim → swimming*.

rows.note: two people → were; dance → dancing (drop the e)

id.note: dua orang → were; dance → dancing (buang e-nya)

blocks.text: Quick test: put *he*, *she* or *they* in place of the subject. *My parents* → they → **were**. *My mother* → she → **was**. *Budi and I* → we → **were**.

id.text: Tes cepat: ganti subjeknya dengan *he*, *she* atau *they*. *My parents* → they → **were**. *My mother* → she → **was**. *Budi and I* → we → **were**.

blocks.prompt: Dimas and his friends ___ singing karaoke at ten.
blocks.explain: Dimas and his friends = they (more than one person) → were singing. 'was' is only for one person or thing.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Dimas and his friends ___ singing karaoke at ten.
id.explain: Dimas and his friends = they (lebih dari satu orang) → were singing. 'was' hanya untuk satu orang atau benda.

blocks.text:
It works like *was/were* on their own. **Negative:** add **not**: **wasn't** (= was not), **weren't** (= were not), then the -ing verb: *I wasn't sleeping.* **Question:** put **Was/Were** before the subject: *She was cooking.* → **Was she cooking?** Short answers: **Yes, she was. / No, she wasn't.** To ask about a time, say **What were you doing at …?** (*Kamu sedang apa jam …?*).

No **did** here: was/were already shows the past. *Did you sleeping?* and *Did you was sleeping?* are wrong → **Were you sleeping?** And don't just add a question mark to a normal sentence (*You were sleeping?*), as Indonesian does with *Kamu sedang tidur?*: put **Were** first.

id.text:
Caranya sama seperti *was/were* tanpa kata kerja lain. **Negatif:** tambahkan **not**: **wasn't** (= was not), **weren't** (= were not), lalu kata kerja -ing: *I wasn't sleeping.* **Pertanyaan:** taruh **Was/Were** di depan subjek: *She was cooking.* → **Was she cooking?** Jawaban singkat: **Yes, she was. / No, she wasn't.** Untuk bertanya tentang suatu jam, ucapkan **What were you doing at …?** (*Kamu sedang apa jam …?*).

Di sini tidak pakai **did**: was/were sudah menunjukkan masa lalu. *Did you sleeping?* dan *Did you was sleeping?* itu salah → **Were you sleeping?** Dan jangan hanya menambah tanda tanya pada kalimat biasa (*You were sleeping?*) seperti *Kamu sedang tidur?* dalam bahasa Indonesia: taruh **Were** di depan.

rows.id: Apakah Pak Hasan sedang mengajar jam sembilan? — Ya.

blocks.text: Answer **What were you doing?** with the same tense: **I was …ing**. 'I'm studying' talks about now, and 'Yes, I was' only answers a yes/no question like *Were you studying?*

id.text: Jawab **What were you doing?** dengan bentuk yang sama: **I was …ing**. 'I'm studying' membicarakan sekarang, dan 'Yes, I was' hanya menjawab pertanyaan ya/tidak seperti *Were you studying?*

blocks.prompt: ___ Rina working at the office yesterday afternoon? — No, she wasn't.
blocks.explain: Past continuous questions start with Was/Were. Rina = she (one person) → Was. 'Did' can't go with an -ing verb, and 'Were' is for you/we/they.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: ___ Rina working at the office yesterday afternoon? — No, she wasn't.
id.explain: Pertanyaan past continuous diawali Was/Were. Rina = she (satu orang) → Was. 'Did' tidak bisa dipakai dengan kata kerja -ing, dan 'Were' untuk you/we/they.

material.title: In the middle at that moment

blocks.text:
The past continuous puts you **in the middle** of an action at one moment in the past. Imagine last night: you **started** cooking at 7:30 and **finished** at 8:30. Someone asks *What were you doing at 8?* At 8 you were in the middle: **I was cooking.** That's the main use: **a time point** (*at 8 last night, at 7 this morning, at this time yesterday*) + **was/were + -ing**.

Compare it with the **past simple** you know (*cooked, went*), which tells the **whole** finished action: *Last night I cooked fried rice for my family* (I started and finished it). *At 8 I was cooking* only shows that one moment in the middle: the cooking wasn't finished yet.

id.text:
Past continuous menempatkan kamu **di tengah** sebuah kegiatan pada satu saat di masa lalu. Bayangkan tadi malam: kamu **mulai** memasak jam 7.30 dan **selesai** jam 8.30. Seseorang bertanya *What were you doing at 8?* Jam 8 kamu sedang di tengah kegiatan itu: **I was cooking.** Itulah pemakaian utamanya: **satu titik waktu** (*at 8 last night, at 7 this morning, at this time yesterday*) + **was/were + -ing**.

Bandingkan dengan **past simple** yang sudah kamu kenal (*cooked, went*), yang menceritakan **seluruh** kegiatan yang sudah selesai: *Last night I cooked fried rice for my family* (saya mulai dan menyelesaikannya). *At 8 I was cooking* hanya menunjukkan satu saat di tengahnya: masaknya belum selesai.

rows.en: Last night I cooked fried rice for my family.
rows.id: Tadi malam saya memasak nasi goreng untuk keluargaku.

id.note: seluruh kegiatan, sudah selesai → past simple

rows.en: At 8 I was cooking, so I didn't answer the phone.
rows.id: Jam 8 saya sedang memasak, jadi saya tidak mengangkat telepon.
rows.note: in the middle at 8 → past continuous

id.note: sedang di tengah kegiatan jam 8 → past continuous

rows.en: Rina went to Jakarta last week.
rows.id: Rina pergi ke Jakarta minggu lalu.

rows.en: At 10 a.m. on Monday she was sitting in a meeting.

rows.note: in the middle at 10 a.m. → past continuous

id.note: sedang di tengah kegiatan jam 10 pagi → past continuous

blocks.text: You'll also see sentences like *I was cooking when Budi came.* The *was cooking* part is the longer action in the middle, and *came* is the short action that happened during it. That pattern comes in a later lesson; for now, just recognise it.

id.text: Kamu juga akan melihat kalimat seperti *I was cooking when Budi came.* Bagian *was cooking* adalah kegiatan panjang yang sedang berlangsung, dan *came* adalah kejadian singkat yang terjadi di tengahnya. Pola ini ada di pelajaran berikutnya; untuk sekarang, cukup kenali saja.

blocks.prompt: Pak Hasan: 'I called you at nine last night, but you didn't answer.' Which reply fits best?
options: Sorry, I was taking a shower.
blocks.explain: At nine last night you were in the middle of something, so use was + -ing: I was taking a shower. 'I'm taking' is about now, and 'I take' is a habit.

id.prompt: Pak Hasan: 'I called you at nine last night, but you didn't answer.' Jawaban mana yang paling tepat?
id.explain: Jam sembilan tadi malam kamu sedang di tengah sebuah kegiatan, jadi pakai was + -ing: I was taking a shower. 'I'm taking' tentang sekarang, dan 'I take' itu kebiasaan.
